newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African industrials end buoyed by early Wall St gains.
newsitem.headline: S.African industrials end buoyed by early Wall St gains.

text.p: South African industrial shares ended slightly firmer, riding up on the back of an early rise on Wall Street and retracing the losses seen during most of an active day's trade, dealers said on Thursday.
Wall Street which fell by 20.87 points on Wednesday started up 40 points on Thursday, with dealers saying its cheerful start would probably firm Friday's trade.
The dealers said the market's underlying sentiment remained positive, but added that some local economic data expected to be released on Friday could hold sway on the market's future direction.
The March trade data, money supply and credit extension figures are largely seen as indicators for movements in the interest rates, they added.
The industrial index ended up 10.6 points to finish at 8,425.4, the gold index shed 1.3 points to close at 1,230.5 and the all-share index gained 7.7 points to 7,087.9.
Dealers said volumes were moderate on the day with around 685 million shares traded, adding the market had also taken a breather amid some positive gains since Monday.
While the industrials were responsive to Wall Street the golds remained stunted for most of the day with bullion still resisting any climb up the $340 an ounce level, dealers said.

They said sentiment from poor gold quarterlies, which the market has largely disounted, was still permeating through the nerves of some market players and leading them to shy away from the precious metal.
The June industrial contract was last at 8,270/75 from 8,270 settlement, the gold contract at 871/80 from 868 and the all-share contract at 6,565/90 from 6,583 settlement.
